verdict.rationale: Secureframe documents an in-app user access review workflow. It pulls user data from native and custom integrations or CSV, runs reviews on recurring schedules, and has designated reviewers decide whether to maintain, modify, revoke, or mark out of scope before closing the review. Nothing in the evidence says the completed review artifact is stored in an evidence library, so the story is only partly covered. Missing for 10: documentation that completed UAR artifacts land in the evidence library or audit evidence, explicit reviewer sign-off/attestation records, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, periodic user access reviews run across connected apps in the platform — reviewers sign off in-app and the artifact lands in the evidence library

citations.quote: Run access reviews for your applications directly inside Secureframe... pull user data in automatically through custom and native integrations or via CSV upload.
Designate reviewers per system and use recurring schedules, reminders, and status indicators to keep the process moving.
Reviewers confirm ownership and decide whether access should be maintained, modified, revoked, or marked out of scope at the account level.
Then scope systems, assign reviewers, evaluate access, and close reviews
